prompt: why do kids lie less to grandparents? essay pls

My daughter is 9 and has quit piano, soccer, and Girl Scouts in the span of 18 months. Everyone keeps telling me I'm teaching her to be a quitter if I let her stop. I'm not so sure. Could you write a personal essay, in my voice roughly, about whether letting kids quit things is actually a failure of parenting or something closer to respect? I don't want it to land neatly on either side.
Op-ed, 800 words or so: the case against homework in elementary school is weaker than people think.

I taught 7th grade math for 11 years before leaving for a tech job. The thing nobody tells you is how much of teaching is crowd control dressed up as pedagogy. Write an essay about that gap between what teacher training says the job is and what it actually is day to day. Honest but not bitter, if you can manage it.
Is reading aloud to kids who can already read themselves a waste of time? I keep doing it with my 11 year old and he still wants it. Write it up as an essay, I'm curious what the argument would be.
Make the argument that boredom is the most underrated thing a child can experience. Blog post tone, not preachy.

ok this is kind of a weird ask but I'm a first time dad (son is 4 months) and I've realized I have no idea how my own father learned to be a father, he never talked about it. Can you write an essay about how men learned fatherhood before parenting books and podcasts existed? Like what did they actually have to go on. I think I'm trying to figure out what I'm supposed to be drawing on.
Write an essay examining why grade inflation has proven so politically durable despite near-universal criticism from educators.
What I wish I knew about the teenage years before my kids hit them. Two boys, now 19 and 22. Write it as if I'm passing it on to a friend whose kid just turned 13.

Everyone loves 'growth mindset' but I've watched it turn into a poster on the wall and nothing else at my kids' school. Short essay on how a decent psychological idea gets flattened once it enters schools?
Essay: the strange disappearance of the school librarian.

Something exploring why siblings raised in the same house by the same parents can turn out so radically different. Not the genetics lecture, more about what 'the same house' even means when you're the oldest vs the youngest.

I'm a pediatric occupational therapist. I want a piece for our clinic newsletter (maybe 1000 words) arguing that handwriting instruction still matters even though kids type everything now. The audience is parents, not clinicians, so keep the motor-development stuff accessible. Don't oversell the research, some of it is mixed.
why is it that every generation of parents thinks the next generation is being raised too soft? write me an essay on that

So my kid's school just switched to standards-based grading (1-4 instead of A-F) and the parent meeting about it was chaos, half the room was furious. I actually think the idea makes sense in theory but I also kind of get why people hate it? Like a 3 means 'meets expectations' and that just feels like a C to everyone over 30. Can you write an essay that takes both reactions seriously and tries to figure out what grades are really for in the first place.
Write an opinion piece arguing that schools should stop teaching cursive and start teaching kids how to fill out forms, read a lease, and argue with a customer service rep.

I was homeschooled K-12 in the 2000s, before it was trendy, and I'm now deciding whether to homeschool my own kids. Write a personal essay weighing what I gained and what I think I lost. Things I lost: lunchroom politics, being bad at something in public. Gained: reading for 6 hours a day, a weird closeness with my mom.
Essay arguing gifted programs do more harm to the kids in them than to the kids left out.

Why do we teach history to kids chronologically? It seems backwards to me, starting with the ancient world when they have zero context for anything. I'd love a short essay on whether there's a better order.
Write a personal essay about the moment a parent realizes their child has become someone they wouldn't have chosen as a friend, and loves them anyway.

Teacher shortages get blamed on pay, but nurses and police are underpaid too and their shortages look different. Write an essay that tries to pin down what is specifically wrong with teaching as a job right now.

Is screen time actually the problem or is it just the thing we can measure? 3 kids, I'm exhausted by the guilt. Write something that takes the question seriously without reassuring me just to make me feel better.
I'd love a reflective essay on the ethics of praising children. When does praise stop being encouragement and start being a form of management?
Underrated: the school bus. Essay.

im a senior in high school and my teacher said we could pick any topic for our final essay as long as it argues something. i want to argue that group projects teach the wrong lessons about working with people. can you write a model essay i can look at to see how an argument like that should be built? around 1200 words
Why did so many medieval people go on pilgrimage when it was dangerous, expensive and took years? Write it as an essay. I feel like 'religion' is too easy an answer.
Essay: the Library of Alexandria didn't burn the way you think.
Argue that the printing press was bad for Europe for about 150 years before it was good. Op-ed style, punchy.

My grandmother was one of the women who worked at the Bletchley Park codebreaking operation and she never told any of us until she was 86. Write a personal essay about what it does to a family when a person keeps a secret like that for 60 years out of duty, and what it means that she finally decided to tell.
Write an essay on why the Roman Republic's institutions, which had survived for nearly five centuries, collapsed within roughly one hundred years. Focus on the norms rather than the laws.

I've been on a kick reading about the 1918 flu and the weird thing is how little anyone seemed to remember it afterward? Like it killed more people than the war but there are barely any monuments, barely any novels about it, my great-grandparents lived through it and apparently never mentioned it. Can you write an essay about why some catastrophes get remembered and others just vanish from the collective memory?
what's the most underrated invention of the 1800s and why is it the refrigerator car? write an essay making the case
Blog post: things historians wish the public understood about how little we actually know about most of the past.
People love to say 'history is written by the victors.' Write an essay testing that claim against actual examples. I suspect it's mostly wrong, or at least badly incomplete.

I teach a survey course on early modern Europe. I want a short essay (~900 words) I can assign in week one that makes students feel how strange the 17th century actually was, so they stop reading it as 'people like us but in wigs.' Pick a handful of concrete things: how they experienced time, darkness, pain, distance. Avoid the Enlightenment-progress narrative.
Did ordinary people in the late Roman Empire know the empire was falling? Write about that.
An op-ed arguing that we should rename fewer things and add more plaques instead.
Write something exploring why the Mongols, who conquered more territory than almost anyone, left so few buildings, books, or monuments behind, and what that does to how we judge them.

I'm giving a toast at my dad's 70th and he's a huge Civil War buff. I don't want to give the toast, I want to understand him better first. Could you write an essay about why so many American men of his generation got obsessed with the Civil War specifically? He grew up in Ohio, born 1956, if that helps.
Why did the Aztec empire fall so fast? Essay, not the Cortés hero story.

I visited the Hiroshima Peace Memorial last spring and what struck me most wasn't the museum, it was how ordinary the city around it felt, people jogging, a Starbucks. Write a personal essay on how cities live on top of their worst days.
Write an essay on the history of the weekend. Who actually won it, and how fragile is it?
The Dark Ages weren't dark, fine, everyone knows that now. But write the essay arguing the correction has gone too far and that something real was in fact lost after 500 AD.
How did people tell time before clocks were common, and what did it do to their sense of being late? I'd read a 1500 word essay on that.
Compose an essay assessing whether the Treaty of Versailles deserves its reputation as the cause of the Second World War.

For my history blog: why the Byzantine Empire is the most underrated civilization in Western schooling, and what it would change if we taught it properly. My readers are mostly nerdy adults, not academics, so a bit of wit is welcome.

My family left Ukraine in 1992 when I was six. I've been trying to write about how the history I was taught as a little kid in Kharkiv and the history I was taught in Ohio described the same 20th century in completely incompatible ways. Help me get started: draft an essay about growing up between two official histories.
what did people do with their old people before nursing homes? and was it actually better? essay

Write an essay questioning the idea that the Industrial Revolution made life worse for ordinary workers. I keep hearing it both ways and want someone to actually weigh the evidence on wages, diet, and life expectancy instead of picking a team.
An essay about shipwrecks as time capsules: what the Mary Rose or the Antikythera wreck tell us that no written record could.
